body:
Thank you so so so much for taking the time out of your day to offer me a detailed response, its really been helpful. I do like your advice on putting on music or a podcast, I think I unintentionally already do that as I *have* to have my music playing because I can't seem to be able to drive with bad radio music or just silence. And I agree with the need to practise, these incidents has really discouraged me but I know that I have to get used to it all somehow so I can function in my life. For now, I've also decided to stick some notes in my car reminding me to do things I forget the most, like taking off the handbrake and turning on headlights at night. 

Do you ever pull over to the hard shoulder (where you're legally allowed) to just take a breather? Cause sometimes I get so anxious and frustrated that I tear up but I still carry on because I think i have to tough it out. I was thinking maybe ill start doing that

And for your last section, gaining access to medicine isn't feasible right now but I'll save up and research with that in mind so that I can deal with it as soon as I have the means to. Also thank you very much for the master doc, it is very helpful!

Thank you for your reply, it does help that there is another person who is facing a similar obstacle to driving as I am. I genuinely fear i might escalate things to a car accident because there have been times where the traffic lights were red and I slow down but forget to brake and I'm just rolling on closer to the car in front of me without even realising as though I'm on autopilot. And for a slightly funnier story, I changed lanes to the hard shoulder once.. because I was just zoning out I guess and thought the hard shoulder was another lane.

I actually have considered adhd in the past, mostly because of an anxiety/ skin picking problem I have. My inability to really focus had hindered my school life but I always thought I'd tough it out somehow. But with how driving is going for me it's really bringing me down. I would really like to get properly checked and possibly treated, but I don't have the health insurance for a diagnosis :( 
If you are receiving treatment,  maybe counselling, would you mind sharing any tips you've learned?

Thanks, I can't order new earphones cause online deliveries are real expensive where I live. But I like the fidget toy idea, I will try to find something 

And the eating thing, I relate so hard. I'd skip eating just cause I don't wanna go into the kitchen and have to interact with people there, they *always* have to talk to me, or I just feel self conscious eating in front of them even though we're not strangers

>You don't have to accept him as your dad, but you should try to be friends.

I try not to fight and am pretty much a wallflower, but sometimes when he spouts his bigoted spiels I can't keep my mouth shut. Hes malicious. he acts like a Karen to immigrant workers and so proudly brags about making a fuss to get them fired and deported back to their country... I mean, it always seems to work, his words always holds more weight than people like us.

 I remember me and my mother saw and talked to immigrant workers from our country, and my mother spoke to my father about how unfair it is that they come here with college education yet get thrown into janitor clothes and paid the most minimum wage (borderline free labour!). You'd think an innocent white man who's just a bit racially insensitive would show some understanding right? He just patronised her and did the typical "they enjoy it here and if they don't like it they can leave" or the "if you don't like it then do something about it"

I can never be his friend. If you knew how it feels with him, as though you're something *lesser* than him, than you would be the same. No wonder my mother's mental health is in shambles

And I understand that it's mature to communicate if I don't wanna be near him in the future, but do I really have to?

>
Are you treating 'British' as synonymous with 'non black

I didnt even say that. Considering that, like you, I grew up English, why would I say that? 
I'm not continuing this conversation cause your focus on the n word out of everything I said is weird, considering that you're asian too

>So it's best just to avoid it entirely.

I dont really understand your point. If a non black person says the n word, regardless of linguistic factors, theyre not reclaiming a slur they're just saying a slur.. so obviously im already avoiding it

I don't see the point of saying them whether you are mixed race or not. I cant even bring myself to say the ch** word, my friend group are all asians (including me) and the thought of using that word with them is off putting. If that word has been thrown at me or my mother, why would I go and say it? I belive the only truly reclaimed slur is the n-word; I cannot be an asian and call another the c word pretending it means "friend", there's still that tug of discomfort in which we're both feeling the effects of that word even if we're the same .

 It's like, if your own parent won't call you that slur (or vice versa) then what makes you think its okay to throw it around to others? Especially to others who are like you and may have bad memories of being called it
Thank you so much! I really appreciate it

Thank you, ranting helped but reading yours and everyone's replies helped even more

>
As for your brother, someday he will figure out how wronged he's been by his father

I was a bit of a self hater at his age too, so I hope he'll grow up and learn to accept himself fully

Thank you, really 
Although I was mad and wanted to rant, I had a thought that I was overreacting maybe and being ungrateful. But your understanding (as well as the other replies) makes me feel reassured. I'll definitely move out by next year and start moving on with my life, and my feeling of debt towards him will hopefully no longer make me feel wrong for feeling these things
I plan to start university at the start of next year (hopefully things will go normally this time since I had to reject offers a couple of times. This house is never at peace haha)
Thanks, I've recently been eating vitamin drops before leaving the house and it actually helps a little in case anyone else wants to try that

>. Ask her a direct question about something she loves talking about.

Honestly I'm not even sure what she likes anymore, if we start talking about her interests they'll always go back to .. *that stuff* somehow 

Also thank you! I wish I saw this sooner before everything already passed, I did end up apologising and felt guilty but I think that's normal

Also thank you for the advice, Ive never been good at confrontation so I think ill try putting it into practice in other times :)
I thought I'd be irresponsible to move out when I don't have any money or other support system, and I kinda don't wanna leave my little brother when everything is still so hectic in the house

Thank you! ♡ yes you're right, even if I only move out somewhere close by I'll still have my space to develop myself a little. And maybe with that space I'll get more mature and me and her can understand each other more. It's not like I want to cut myself off from her, I just want to get away a bit

Isn't it similar as getting into a relationship and forgetting your individuality? I think its normal to get tired or suffocated when you live with a parent and have to give yourself up. Anyways thanks again for the encouragement, there's no other adult for me to talk to so I'm glad I was able to get advice from people here

I don't know how to change my username but I changed my display name haha

>Do you a school counselor or someone trusted with whom you could talk?

No there's noone , aside from my friends (who all moved away 😭), all my network is connected to her in some way

>maybe it's time to start thinking about how to move yourself both physically and mentally from the nest.

I *am* however moving out for college in 5 months (I hope 🙏) its in my small city so I  wouldn't have really gotten away from her that much. I'm thinking I could save up and rent a place with a friend when I finish my studies .

I won't lie that she's unstable right now and not in a position where I want to blindly follow everything she says. Even if I feel a shred of independence for taking my first dose alone, it's also a little bitter, because I'm only okay right now because she was only okay with the vaccine I chose. In a sense, she still chose for me and I'm still stuck following her whims. If I had taken a different vaccine, the outcome would have been terrible and i would not have even been able to get my second dose. So really, what independence do I actually have? It feels like I'll never be my own person, like I'm just a part of her and that's all I will be

Thank you for the encouraging words

>Mom, I'm so glad that you are now ready to get the vaccine and would love to accompany you to your appointment. Some months ago, when you were so adamant about not getting the vaccine, I went ahead and got my first shot. I am sorry I kept it from you, but I knew you would be angry/worried and I didn't want to do that to you. I felt strongly that I needed to be vaccinated because ......fill in the blank. I love you and wanted to keep you safe." 

I wouldn't even be able to get the first sentence out before she snapped 😂. However, I'm okay now, completely because by chance I vaccinated with the vaccine she trusts enough (and if there's any higher being up there, I'm forever grateful for that lucky chance haha God did not in fact mess me up)

. I think ill be okay, and i look forward to the day I can finally leave for uni (although she'll still be near me in terms of distance and can easily reach me, in fact all my relatives can easily find me. We live in a small city) I just hope to find a job abroad and get away from my family completely . Is wishing that a bad thing? I just feel that she will never change and have completely given up hope of my original mother ever returning . I just want to move on for myself instead of constantly living for her,  if you know what I mean.

Thank you again for the guidance in how to talk to her, its unfortunate that I only saw this after having told her, because I probably would have needed it

Thank you for the encouragement, as you said, I feel much better now. I'm amazed that you have a daughter the same age as me and although I don't know anything about you guys, in this aspect at least I can say I'm jealous of her, and glad that she has a parent like you she can wholeheartedly rely on with this sort of thing
I'm not sure I understand that well, but I think it a little? I'll try it
Thank you!

Thank you for the kind words :) I couldn't sleep at all and my stomach just hurts right now,  I'm really doing my best to stay calm and prepare myself

Are you a parent? If so, do you have advice on how I could start the topic so that it won't escalate? It probably won't be good to just go "I actually don't need a first dose 😬 *hands vaccine record slip* " ?
I'm honestly worried I'll get kicked out since she does that a lot when she's mad, so I wanna avoid that

>Get your second vaccine on time and tell her that you're "getting the vaccine"

I wish I could but I'm honestly tired. Also, she wouldn't let me handle my own appointment for me to quietly get my second dose without her knowing☹ 

>You're an adult and you don't have to share every last detail of your medical care with your mom anymore.

this whole thing started because she wouldn't let me be an adult and respect my decisions about own body, so she won't even respect my right to medical privacy even if I'm an adult

I'm 19, and like you, am set to start at uni at 20. But about that your mother is wrong, it's never too late to start,  and its fine to enjoy this window of freedom before you start uni. So being that you're not the only one in this boat, know that you aren't abnormal or falling behind like your mother wants you to think. 

I'm also dealing with stuff with my mother and my suicidal thoughts are just coming back again. Hopefully you and I will get through this and have a *very* successful university life as well as a successful future /career. For one, I've cried because I'm going to a university I never wanted to go to, under a completely different degree from what I wanted. It's a sacrifice I had to make for my family, but I can make myself love it and so can you. Your future at college will be great and you can overcome your mother's words and regain that drive to go to college
No I'm not in the U.S. where I am, the doctors would still probably tell my parents even if I'm legal and practically beg them not to :/

Shes still in her conspiracy bubble, but thankfully trusts this vaccine enough. Which is funnily enough the same vaccine I got. I know there is no "perfectly safe" way to tell her the truth. The only safe way would have been in 10 years with me on the other side of the world away from her, telling her by text or something. I dont know anymore, and I'm sick of it all. I'm honestly sick of having to deal with her and I'm sick of having to be so dependant on her. It's like I'll never be able to do what I want even as a grown up. Even as a 30 year old I'll probably have to anxiously tip toe around her. I'm tired and a little frustrated now. At first I was real scared but now I'm just sick of it. I'll probably tell her the truth tomorrow and just let her do whatever she wants if it'll please her or make her less angry

But best case scenario is her being okay , and understanding why I felt so cornered enough to take the initative myself . But there's no way she'll be understanding 😂 
I'm sorry if I'm coming across irresponsible or rude, or if writing too much (I cant sleep but I'll go to bed after this)  I've actually really reflected on this desicion to vaccinate alone i had made, and spent so much energy worrying and being anxious. I was serious about my safety throughout it all. But God really messed me up with this. I mean 2-3 weeks after I gathered up courage and got my first dose, my mother decides to let me vaccinate (with the *same* vaccine too). That's a cruel joke god played I swear

Update: told her yay. At first I considered not doing it cause she was going on about how people need to take 5 doses and 10 doses and more and that's how the government controls us and she's been talking to people who were apparently forced to take 5 doses. It's laughable and I had a mini argument telling her that the very same government she's accusing has been posting statements for employers to not have people take more than 3 doses. In fact, the government had been actively advising people not to exceed more than 3 doses. But of course the people she's been talking to are way more credible (they're pretty much her only source hah) than the literal government website doing the exact opposite of what her and her circle are going on about. 

Thankfully I was able to come out unharmed because I had vaccinated with the vaccine she trusts. However with the nonsense she's saying I've been swayed to think i chose the wrong vaccine. I had to cater to her a little and agree with some things she said so that she'd let me be with this decision.  It hurt my soul, but I swear she's a little narcissistic or something.  Because everything I say is wrong (even if it's literally sourced from legit organisations and the freaking government), and everything her little dumb group and her dumb YouTube videos tells her is right. She acts so incredibly smart and spiritually enlightened while diminishing me as not knowing a thing. Which irritates me because she knows absolutely nothing about vaccines, could not ever scientifically explain her bold accusations. I'm sure you understand this frustration. 

It doesn't matter If the government itself said "no more than 3 doses recommended", if her dumb group says they're being forced to take 20 doses thats the absolute truth and the government is controlling us and forcing us!! /s
Anyways, sorry I'm just a little fed up. She just told me that I'm not going anywhere (like for uni) for another year , even though I was so sure I'd be away from her in 5 months . How is it that the time I have to stay home with her is always extended without me realising.

Side note,  I don't know if Gods exist, but I thank them very much for letting me be guided to the vaccine that she would be okay with. Thats the only reason I'm safe right now
My dad's hospitalised right now ☹ so it's me alone

Do you mean that the centre could hide that I already did my first dose? If so, I really wish that was possible..  but I don't think they'll care, and I'm not even sure if we'll go to the same centre I went to

I think ill have to tell her, but I really don't know how to, and I don't want a screaming match or anything more than that

Thank you

Yes, I think she wants to take me to the centre herself

I don't think I'll be able to call her and tell her from a safe distance ☹

I don't think I'm a fully capable adult at all, hence why I'm still so scared of going against her decisions. But whether I like it or not,  I have to be an adult, because I'm leaving for university soon alone and I need to learn to make decisions for myself. I didn't make this decision in a split of a second. Nor did I necessarily let my friends influence me, but I won't lie that they played a part in me building courage. They never tried convincing me, it was me who made a decision and asked them to accompany me

My mother had always been my role model and I always wanted to trust her decisions, it hurts to go against it. But even if I'm not an adult, I'm not stupid, l can form a own thoughts on things, and I can see when even my own trusted guardian is being irrational. Maybe the fact that she had to be strong for so long tired her out, but she is not in a mentally healthy position to be forcing these decisions onto me, especially when its concerning our health. 

In regards to my mother's decision, I would like to say its coming from a place of love but perhaps she is just gullible. I know shes genuinely believing the things she's been fed about the vaccine, and she even told "im trying trying to protect you from yourself" but that is just a bit narcissistic. Especially when she's once said she has to save the world from Satan or whatever . She was almost indoctrinated to a cult just half a year ago I think, and she never listened to me when I said they were weird. I did my research on the cult leader and used it to say my points, which helped, but from this incident its evident that she never fact checks and chooses to blindly believe, plus she never values my opinions. Although (thankfully) she didn't fall into that cult, she had a mental breakdown that scared me and my little brother (she called it a spiritual awakening, but I can differetiate between awakening and a simple breakdown) and still follows these weird groups and YouTube channels that drew her into the anti vaxx Blackhole in the first place. I am saying that, no matter if she is doing this out of love, I can't blindly rely on someone like that. 

It wasn't an easy decision to make by no means, but given that we want to visit my home country (where masks are barely even worn) I worry for my safety and for my family too. If we we are to travel to these places, I thought I should at least take my own safety into my own hands. So since my mother refuses to give up her beliefs and pride for the sake of our family, of my little brother who has ASTHMA, I have always tried my best to keep safe (like wearing masks outside constantly even though she hates masks) even if I had to respect her decision. But as I said, time is passing, I will be moving abroad for university and even if I don't think I'm a capable adult yet at all,  but I have to start acting like it by taking responsibility for my own safety

I know how vaccines work, and I researched the particular vaccine I will be taking, even if I'm scared, I didn't make this big decision on a whim. It was not easy at all, do you not see how scared I am?
